metadata.title: Secure Container Platform

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for operating container platforms that preserve isolation, integrity, and trust across build, runtime, host, and orchestration layers.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Container platforms, runtimes, host operating systems, orchestration environments, and associated control planes.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Composite pattern asserting that foundational container trust, runtime isolation, host OS security, orchestration governance, and supply-chain integrity requirements are satisfied.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Container runtime isolation, orchestration security, host OS hardening, image supply chain trust, secrets handling, and monitoring expectations defined by NIST SP 800-190.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Privilege escalation impacting container runtimes, host operating systems, or orchestration control planes.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Lateral movement across container workloads, shared nodes, or orchestrated services.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Initial access via compromised container images, secrets, or orchestration interfaces.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Container escape affecting host systems and all resident workloads.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Supply chain compromise of container images or build pipelines.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Execution and workload isolation across containerized environments.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Integrity validation of container artifacts and dependencies.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Reduction of attack surface across host OS, runtime, and orchestration control planes.

metadata.remarks: Secure Container Platform is a composite trust pattern asserting that container execution, runtime isolation, host OS security, secrets management, orchestration governance, and supply-chain integrity requirements are collectively satisfied. It introduces no independent controls and exists solely as an aggregate trust claim for solution patterns, SSPPs, and system security and privacy documentation.
